CloudHQ MCC2 is a data center building on CloudHQ's MCC Campus in the Manassas data center submarket of Prince William County, Virginia, near Manassas Regional Airport on the south side of the city of Manassas. The MCC Campus is CloudHQ's original campus and, per the operator's own current campus page, spans 2,232,875 square feet and totals 382 megawatts of critical IT load across seven buildings numbered MCC1 through MCC7, with 96 megawatts of that total still available for new tenants as of the operator's most recently published figures. CloudHQ describes MCC1 through MCC4 as already operational and together carrying the bulk of the campus's more than 375 megawatts of deployed critical load, MCC5 as site plan approved and ready for immediate development, and MCC7 as beginning construction in mid 2025 with an expected ready for service date in the third quarter of 2026. The operator's page does not break these figures out building by building, so the campus-wide capacity total is not applied to MCC2 individually in this record, and CloudHQ has not published a confirmed street address for MCC2 on its current public site. The campus connects to CloudHQ's adjacent MDC campus and to regional and long haul fiber routes the company markets as the Manassas Fiber Highway.

CloudHQ was founded in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, who earlier founded QTS Realty Trust and who, according to the company's own materials, was the first person in the United States to obtain an IRS ruling permitting data center income to qualify for real estate investment trust tax treatment. The company operates as part of the Fateh Family Office alongside affiliated entities CloudCapital, WindHQ, and Dalian Development, and keeps its global headquarters at 1212 New York Avenue in Washington DC, with regional offices in London and Singapore. CloudHQ states it employs more than 330 people and describes its global footprint as 23 campuses spanning more than 30 million square feet across six countries, with more than 1,380 megawatts of critical IT load already contracted and roughly 6,000 megawatts of expansion potential identified across its current land holdings. The company is a founding member of the Data Center Coalition and participates in national data center trade associations in the United Kingdom, Brazil, Mexico, and Germany, among others.

Prince William County has become one of Northern Virginia's fastest growing data center submarkets over the past decade, expanding outward from the much larger Loudoun County cluster centered on Ashburn. The county has approved a series of large rezoning and special use permit applications for data center campuses along its Manassas and Gainesville corridors, and has also seen organized community opposition to some of the larger proposed campuses near residential neighborhoods and the Manassas National Battlefield Park. This record does not tie CloudHQ's MCC Campus to any specific named zoning docket or county approval, since no county planning record naming MCC2 by address was located this session.
